citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825.
creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech; Databricks Mosaic)
description: CommonCatalog-C is a dataset of approximately 26 million Creative-Commons-licensed images sourced from YFCC100M (via Flickr), restricted to images licensed for commercial use (CC-BY and CC-BY-SA licenses). Each image is paired with a high-quality synthetic caption generated by a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. It is a subset of the larger CommonCatalog-NC dataset and was curated to train open text-to-image diffusion models without relying on web-scraped data of unclear copyright provenance.
name: CommonCatalog-C
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2-generated captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than corresponding LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions. Quantitatively, BLIP-2 captions achieve higher CLIP Scores than ground-truth captions (corroborated by Nguyen et al.), at the cost of reduced caption diversity as measured by unique trigrams. Approximately 30.76% of CommonCatalog-C images had existing alt-text captions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Captions were synthesized using the telephoning method: a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model was applied to each CC image to generate a synthetic caption. BLIP-2 was chosen based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. The captioning process required approximately 1,120 GPU A100 hours. About 30.76% of CommonCatalog-C images had existing alt-text captions.
rai:dataBiases: The YFCC100M source data is approximately a decade old, making the CC images less current than those in LAION-2B. Synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions. Models trained on CommonCatalog underperformed in categories including faces, general photography, and paintings — categories originating from the Conceptual Captions dataset which relies on web-scraped data. The dataset is limited to images from Flickr users who chose CC licenses, which may not be representative of all image types.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the YFCC100M dataset by re-scraping from Flickr using the Flickr IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Only images with Creative-Commons licenses that permit commercial use (CC-BY 2.0 and CC-BY-SA 2.0) and do not restrict derivative works were retained. Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The resulting CommonCatalog-C dataset contains approximately 26,232,417 images.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data is the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files with associated Flickr IDs. Images were re-scraped from Flickr at very high resolution (exceeding 4K). The YFCC100M images are approximately a decade old.
rai:dataLimitations: The YFCC100M source data is approximately a decade old and its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. Only roughly 70 million usable CC images were found, which is far fewer than the billions of images in LAION used to train SD2. Synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 have reduced n-gram diversity. Models trained on this data underperform in categories such as faces, general photography, and paintings. Although trained on CC images, adversarial prompts can still produce content resembling iconic characters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered by Creative-Commons license type: images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. For caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels before being passed to BLIP-2. At training time, all images remain in their native resolution. Images were further divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) subsets based on their license.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset provides a path toward training high-quality text-to-image models without relying on web-scraped data of unclear copyright provenance, addressing ongoing copyright lawsuits related to generative AI training. By using only Creative-Commons-licensed images with known provenance, it enables greater reproducibility and avoids link rot issues. The dataset also demonstrates that models trained on CC data are less likely to generate iconic copyrighted characters compared to models trained on LAION.
rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image generative diffusion models using only open-licensed, Creative-Commons data. The dataset is intended as an alternative to web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B for training high-quality T2I models while avoiding copyright concerns. It can also be used for research on data-efficient training of generative models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained image-to-text model) was used to generate synthetic captions for all CC images in the dataset.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of people, including public figures and celebrities, sourced from Flickr. No explicit anonymization or removal of personal information is described.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image receives exactly one synthetic caption from BLIP-2; no multiple independent annotations per item are described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Captions are generated by an automated ML model (BLIP-2), not human annotators; no human annotator demographics are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No human annotation platform used; captions were generated automatically by BLIP-2.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is stated in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; missing captions are handled by generating synthetic ones rather than imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described; paper mentions future plans to augment with other CC sources but no formal maintenance plan.
